title: Retrieval-time valid-time gating over a clause-level, recency-decoupled amended-regulation benchmark
research_question: Does enforcing valid-time (as-of) membership post hoc at retrieval time reduce clause-level point-in-time retrieval failures and version contamination - compared with semantic-only retrieval, elapsed-time decay, a hard as-of filter, and a retriever adapted to temporal context - and is the effect consistent across sparse, dense and hybrid retrievers; and does it improve answer accuracy on the subset of queries where retrieving a non-gold version would change the answer?
hypothesis: A single post-hoc valid-time (as-of) gate applied unchanged across sparse, dense and hybrid retrievers reduces clause-level point-in-time retrieval failures and version contamination relative to semantic-only retrieval, elapsed-time decay and a hard as-of filter, and the gain is concentrated on strata where the in-force version is not the latest; the effect is reported per retriever whether or not it is consistent across them, and answer accuracy improves only on the answer-differential subset.
proposed_method: Reconstruct clause version chains and per-clause validity intervals from amendment metadata; build version-identity-labelled queries with recency-decoupled strata and an answer-differential screen. Apply the temporal gate post hoc to each base retriever's candidate list (BM25, dense, hybrid RRF) in four signal forms, with a date-conditioned/fine-tuned retriever as a representation-level comparator. Report per-retriever effects as the primary result rather than a pooled average, and characterize the recency-decay hybrid that is the published state of the art.
baselines: Semantic-only retrieval per base retriever (BM25, dense, hybrid RRF) with no temporal term
Recency/elapsed-time decay re-ranking with tuned decay rate
Published fixed three-signal hybrid (lexical + dense + decay)
Retriever adapted to temporal context (date-conditioned or fine-tuned dense retriever)
Recency-only ranker (always prefer the latest version), reported per stratum
Random temporal assignment control (random validity intervals)
datasets: Primary: a public versioned legal/regulatory corpus with clause-level amendment metadata and machine-readable validity dates (e.g. consolidated EU legislation with European Legislation Identifier entry-into-force and applicability dates), snapshotted on a fixed date
Primary query set: time-stamped questions constructed from clause version chains, oversampled on the non-latest-gold stratum, with an answer-differential subset

Reusable infrastructure: the public RMA regulatory QA benchmark harness (sparse/dense/hybrid arms with ROUGE/BERTScore and no-answer rate, https://github.com/PravaatChhetri/rma-rag-benchmark) for retrieval and evaluation plumbing, but its corpus is static with no versioning or target dates, so the corpus and label pipeline must be replaced
Not used: TemporalESG and the trilingual ESG benchmark (accessibility and domain mismatch), SituatedQA/TimeQA (web QA, not clause-versioned)
metrics: Primary: clause-level point-in-time recovery - fraction of queries whose top-ranked or cited passage was in force at the target date
Primary: version contamination - fraction of retrieved passages not in force at the target date
Primary: version confusion - fraction of queries whose selected version differs from the gold version
Co-primary: answer accuracy (EM/F1 or judged equivalence) on the answer-differential subset only
Diagnostic: nDCG@k and Recall@k against version-identity gold labels
Diagnostic: abstention rate when no version is in force at the target date
Interaction: per-retriever effect sizes and whether the sign is consistent across retrievers
reproducibility_notes: Correction to the earlier version of this plan: an open implementation does exist for static regulatory-document QA (the RMA benchmark repository, publicly released with evaluation scripts), but it contains no temporal, versioning or target-date labels, so it cannot be run to test this hypothesis and no execution spec is attached; it can be reused for retrieval/evaluation plumbing only. When the version-level benchmark is built: pin and document the corpus snapshot date and amendment metadata source, publish version chains and validity intervals, fix all seeds, hold the reader/prompt/decoding fixed, publish the answer-differential screening procedure and query-stratum assignments, release per-query predictions so every metric can be recomputed, report per-retriever effects and paired bootstrap confidence intervals, and report both natural-prevalence-weighted and oversampled-stratum estimates to avoid overstating the deployment impact.
